title: Move NERV's FPV data to FPVBuddy behind its MCP server; NERV keeps no FPV data or code
goal: Batteries, fleet, spares, crashes, FPV builds and their history and photos live in FPVBuddy, reached over its MCP server, with nothing lost
acceptance: A one-time export from NERV's store and import into FPVBuddy moves batteries, fleet, spares, crashes, FPV builds and manufacturer docs with their history (resistance readings, cycles, crash-to-battery-damage links); verified by per-table counts on both sides and a sample of records compared field by field; the export file and owner data never enter Git
Photos attached to batteries, crashes and parts (src/photos.ts ownerKind battery, crash, part) stay linked: moved with the data or referenced by FPVBuddy IDs, with an ID map kept outside Git

Durability: FPVBuddy's data has a backup or replication story at least as good as NERV's store (NERV-01/NERV-02 replication), named in this record, or the owner accepts a recorded gap before the import
The migration is a script with a dry run and a test on invented data; it refuses to run twice over the same data

Owner decision 2026-11-26 (chat): "Drop F-101-T05, and add a step to move your battery data to FPVBuddy, behind its MCP server." NERV never imports the FPV core; it reaches FPVBuddy over MCP only (coordinator docs/DOMAINS.md; coordinator:F-016 shared-assets rule). F-101-T09 (storage reminders), F-101-T10 (every FPV tool keeps a path, unreachable FPVBuddy) and F-101-T11 (removal) complete the move.
privacy: Owner fleet data stays local-only and never enters Git; tests use invented batteries, drones, crashes and photos.
escalation: A material scope or effort increase goes to the owner
A durability gap, or importing owner data on a machine not recorded, goes to the owner before the import

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-26 after the owner decision (export and import script with a dry run, count and sample check, photo ID map). Not a measurement.
